claims.text: An Al2O3 coating can improve the oxygen resistance of equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The coating should be 1–2 μm thick.
The applied Al2O3 coating provides an Al2O3 surface layer.
The Al2O3 layer prevents oxygen diffusion into equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr.
At 800 °C in air for 5 h without external loading, the coating will reduce the oxidation rate by 50% relative to untreated material, as measured by weight gain.
The untreated comparison material is equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed protection is applicable from 600 to 1000 °C in air or other oxygen-rich environments for exposures of 1–10 h.
The proposed protection is applicable under no external loading or moderate stresses below 100 MPa.
Oxidation-rate reduction may depend on coating thickness, uniformity, adhesion, and test conditions.
A controlled oxidation experiment will compare weight gain and microstructure of coated and untreated samples after 5 h in air at 800 °C.
The hypothesis is falsified if the coated sample's weight gain is not at least 30% lower than that of the untreated sample after 5 h in air at 800 °C.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome specifies a 50% oxidation-rate reduction, whereas the hypothesis is only falsified below a 30% reduction. A result between 30% and 49% would fail the quantitative prediction but would not falsify the hypothesis under the stated rule.
